o.text:
From Proto-Turkic *arka.
Cognates
Cognate with
Turkmen and
Turkish arka,
Uzbek orqa (“back”),
Uyghur ئارقا (arqa, “back”),
Tatar and
Kyrgyz арка (arka, “back”),
Kazakh арқа (arqa, “back”),
Bashkir арҡа (arqa, “back”),
Crimean Tatar arqa (“back”),
Yakut арҕаа (arğaa, “west; back”) and Yakut арҕас (arğas, “mane of a horse”)
Shor арға (“ridge, range; side; pointiness”),
Tuvan арга (arga, “mountain forest”);
Chuvash урхалӑх (urh̬alăh) / орхалӑх (orh̬alăh, “saddle girth”), from obsolete Chuvash орха (orh̬a, “back”).
Borrowed from Russian эколо́гия (ekológija), from German Ökologie.
From Persian برپا (barpâ, “afoot”). The modern senses probably developed under semantic influence of the Russian восстановле́ние (vosstanovlénije).
From qıvır- + -aq. Cognate with Turkish kıvrak.

From qüvvət (“strength”) + -siz.
Cognate with Bashkir ҡеүәтһеҙ (qiwäthið), Kazakh қуатсыз (quwatsız), Tatar куәтсез (quwätsez), Turkish kuvvetsiz, Turkmen kuwwatsyz, Uyghur قۇۋۋەتسىز (quwwetsiz), Uzbek quvvatsiz.
